input.question: If Germany wasn't a country at the time, how come Martin Luther was considered German? What nationality would he have been considered at the time?
input.ground_truth: Germanic was an ethnic group long before the company of Germany was formed. Germany is really just the latest iteration in a chain of German countries in that area of the world. The Holy Roman Empire was the first "germany", but even before that the Romans would refer to that part of the world as Germania.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If Germany wasn't a country at the time, how come Martin Luther was considered German? What nationality would he have been considered at the time?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big family, but right now, your family hasn’t decided on a family name yet. So, you don’t really have a “family” in the way we think of countries today.

Martin Luther was like that. He lived in a place that we now call Germany, but back then, that place didn’t have one big country name like “Germany.” Instead, it was made up of lots of little groups and areas, kind of like different rooms in a big house.

So, Martin Luther didn’t say, “I’m German,” because that name wasn’t used for countries yet. But people knew he was from that part of the world. They might have said he was from “Saxony” (the area where he lived) or called him a “Saxon” or maybe just said he was from “the Holy Roman Empire,” which was the big group of areas that included his home.

So, he didn’t have a country called Germany, but people still knew where he came from!
